text:
maria: incident-bot paged me for repeated SLA latency alerts for tenant=brightpath :rotating_light: — 90% p95 > 600ms across api-gen routes. Not seeing obvious infra OOMs.
incident-bot: [ALERT] tenant_sla_latency_high brightpath count=37 threshold=3m
maria: quick triage: checked node CPU/GPU, KV cache hit rates normal, but saw a spike in long-tail seq lengths from user traffic. Likely workload pattern change.
liam: pinged on-call infra to see if any autoscale throttles were blocking burst capacity. @alex any routing changes in the last 30m?
alex: no config/API rollouts. We had a canary model swap earlier but only for internal model-id=redwood-v1-cand. Not targetting brightpath.
maya: I'm seeing a lot of noisy tenant heartbeats for brightpath from our synthetic checks — they send batch requests often. Could be synthetic flooding + app workload.
maria: paging frequency is noisy. Suggest we suppress immediate paging to reduce toil while we investigate. Propose: mute the SLA-policy alert for tenant=brightpath for 30m and create a separate non-paging alert on aggregated error budget.
liam: agree. I'll take the handoff and mute. Oncall cmd: `./srectl alerts mute --alert-id tenant_sla_latency_high --filter "tenant=brightpath" --duration 30m`
liam: muting now... `OK: alert muted (id=mute-789)` :white_check_mark:
liam: also creating a short-lived dashboard: grafana link: https://grafana.company/ d/abcd/brightpath-incident to look at token-level latencies, batch sizes, seq lengths, and route breakdowns.
jenn: added a temporary panel for seq_length distribution and model cache KV-miss count. Early signal: brightpath traffic shows increased avg_seq_len from 512->1400 around the spike.
maria: that explains p95. Two mitigation paths: (1) contact customer to throttle or apply client-side batching limit, (2) change per-tenant soft threshold so alert triggers on QPS-normalized latency instead of absolute p95.
liam: for immediate customer impact—are SLAs breached? We saw a couple of user-facing timeouts but not full outage. Need to mark as 'potentially degraded' for Brightpath.
maya: I'll open a support ticket and ping AE to check customer-side config. Ticket created: https://tickets/BR-4021
liam: actionable follow-ups:
- create a non-paging synthetic that tracks seq_len distribution (owner: maya)
- change alert to `tenant_sla_latency_high_v2` to be QPS-weighted with a higher absolute threshold for seq_len>1024 (owner: alex)
- add a Grafana panel and an automatic runbook link (owner: jenn)
maria: I'll add this to post-incident tuning doc and schedule an alerts sweep for tenant-specific heartbeats tomorrow at 10am.
liam: adding tasks to the oncall board now. Also enabling a temporary scaling profile for brightpath for 1h: `infractl scale --pool=dedicated-brightpath --factor=1.5 --until=1h` — applied.
alex: scaling looked good, latency dropped ~30% in 8 minutes. P95 back to ~420ms.
maria: nice. we should keep the mute until we confirm traffic patterns stabilize. I'll hand off to liam for the next 2h watch.
liam: taking handoff. will monitor dashboards and coordinate with maya on the ticket. @sre-bot log: incident_type=tenant-noisy-sla, impact=degraded, mitigation=muted-alert+scale, followups=alerts-sweep+dashboard
maria: thanks — leaving channel. :wave:
liam: copying runbook snippet for postmortem and tuning (put this in the follow-up doc):
```
1) Identify tenant causing noise (query: `sum by (tenant) (rate(api_latency_ms_bucket[5m]))`)
2) Check seq_len and batch-size distribution
3) If synthetic heartbeat noise, convert to non-paging alert and move to aggregated metric
4) If customer traffic change, contact AE & suggest client-side rate limiting or model param changes
5) Update alert: use QPS-normalized threshold, and add seq_len gating to avoid blind pages
```
liam: will update thread with the postmortem link once complete. monitoring: keeping the non-paging alert active so we don't lose signal. :thumbsup:
